repro: POST https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/digest/unsubscribe with NO Authorization header and body {"userId":"not-a-uuid"}
Observe 400 (a zod validation error), NOT 401 — the request reached the handler, so the route has no authentication gate at all
apps/api/src/routes/digest.ts:31 registers server.post('/unsubscribe', ...) with no preHandler and no authenticateUser
Its body schema (digest.ts:25) is {userId: z.string().uuid(), reason?: string} — the caller names the victim
digest.ts:46 then INSERTs that userId into WeeklyDigestOptOut with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, and jobs/weekly-digest.ts:238 reads that table to suppress the send
The ids are in circulation: jobs/weekly-digest.ts:471 builds the email link as /account/digest/unsubscribe?u=<raw user.id>, and GET /auth/me returns the caller's own id verbatim
I did NOT execute the write against any real user id — that would mutate a record I did not create
findings.observed: The endpoint is anonymous and takes the target user's raw primary key as its only parameter, so anyone holding or enumerating a Darshya user UUID can silently opt that user out of the weekly digest. It is also one-way: WeeklyDigestOptOut is only ever INSERTed (digest.ts:46) or SELECTed (weekly-digest.ts:238) — no route in the API deletes a row, so neither the victim nor support can re-subscribe them through the product. There is no sensitiveRateLimit on this route either, unlike account.ts:178 and :287 which do carry it, so the user table can be walked.
findings.expected: A one-click unsubscribe link should carry a signed, per-user, single-purpose token (an HMAC of the user id and a secret, RFC 8058 style) rather than the raw primary key, so that possessing an id is not the same as possessing the authority to act on it. The opt-out should also be reversible — a re-subscribe path so a mistaken or malicious opt-out can be undone.
findings.evidence: Unauthenticated POST /digest/unsubscribe {"userId":"not-a-uuid"} -> HTTP 400 {"error":"Invalid request."}. A 400 rather than a 401 is the proof: the handler ran. Same 400 for an empty body and for no body at all.

repro: POST /bookings/5902e915.../cancel again -> 409 'Booking cannot be cancelled in its current status cancelled.' (correct)
GET /bookings/5902e915.../cancel-quote -> 200 with cancellationAllowed true and refundAmountInr 1152
findings.observed: After the booking is cancelled, the quote endpoint still answers cancellationAllowed:true and offers a full 1152 refund on a booking the cancel endpoint will refuse with 409. Root cause: devoteeCancelAllowed() (apps/api/src/services/cancellation.service.ts:83) tests only hoursUntilSlot plus an early return for pending_payment; it never checks for a terminal status such as cancelled or completed.
findings.expected: cancellationAllowed:false with the refund figures zeroed, matching what POST /cancel will actually do. The endpoint's own comment block (routes/bookings.ts:1864-1881) says this flag exists precisely so the quote and the executor can never disagree — the LEG-03 defect. That guarantee holds for the time-cutoff case but not for the status case. Not user-visible on web today: app/bookings/view/page.tsx:856 gates the Cancel button on statusIsCancellable, so the dialog that fetches the quote cannot open on a cancelled booking. It is an API-contract defect that any other client (mobile, a retry, a direct caller) can still hit.

repro: GET /bookings/79337475-93eb-4ab8-b0ef-44a82a9b8295 -> the stored name is 10,000 characters, untruncated
GET that booking -> devoteeNames is [{"name":"  "}], a booking with a blank devotee
findings.observed: createBookingSchema (apps/api/src/routes/bookings.ts:85-88) validates the devotee name with z.string().min(1) and nothing else — no .max() and no .trim(). A 10,000-character name is persisted in full, and a whitespace-only string satisfies min(1), so a booking can be made with no readable devotee name at all. The name is the sankalp identity: it is rendered on the booking page, on the pandit's job card, and in the WhatsApp booking templates, none of which have a length budget for 10k characters. sankalpDetails and specialInstructions on the same schema are likewise unbounded.
findings.expected: A .trim() before the min(1) check so two spaces is rejected as empty, and a sane .max() on the name and the two free-text fields beside it.
findings.evidence: 201 {"booking":{"id":"79337475-93eb-4ab8-b0ef-44a82a9b8295","bookingNumber":"BS-20260908-DVZZN"}} then GET /bookings/79337475... -> first devotee name length 10000. And 201 {"bookingNumber":"BS-20260908-KSR9M"} whose devoteeNames read back as [{"name":"  "}].

repro: POST /bookings/book with scheduledTimeSlot '99:99' and everything else valid
-> 409 {"error":"The selected time slot is no longer available.","code":"SLOT_UNAVAILABLE"}
findings.observed: A syntactically impossible time is reported as a capacity conflict. scheduledTimeSlot is only z.string().min(1), so 99:99 passes schema validation and is caught later by the availableSlots membership test, which owns the 'no longer available' copy. The devotee is told to try another time because this one filled up, when the request was in fact malformed and no such time exists.
findings.expected: A 400 with a format error (the slot must match HH:MM and be one of the offering's availableSlots), reserving SLOT_UNAVAILABLE / 409 for a well-formed slot that is genuinely taken. The request IS correctly rejected either way and no booking is created, so this is copy accuracy only.
findings.evidence: 409 {"error":"The selected time slot is no longer available.","code":"SLOT_UNAVAILABLE","message":"चुना गया समय स्लॉट अब उपलब्ध नहीं है।"} for slot 99:99. Contrast: slot '' -> 400 'Time slot is required'.
